Direct evidence for the exact setting—sequential recommendation, random text initialization, and explicit model-number/unit/negation/compatibility tests—is missing from the studies located. Mean pooling of context-free token embeddings is permutation-invariant: it retains token presence but loses number–unit associations and negation scope. Small CNNs can represent local ordered phrases, although this does not guarantee attribute understanding. [ConvMF](https://dsail.kaist.ac.kr/files/RecSys16.pdf) provides relevant indirect evidence: randomly initialized, jointly learned CNN text features improved rating prediction over bag-of-words document models; Amazon Instant Video RMSE was 1.1337 versus 1.3594 for CDL. This is neither a mean-pooling ablation nor sequential HR@10 evidence.

[Ask the GRU](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.02116v2) directly compares an order-sensitive text encoder against an averaged-embedding encoder: CiteULike cold-start Recall@50 improved from 38.53% to 46.16%, and from 35.85% to 47.59%. Its scientific-paper setting does not establish product-attribute preservation. For ID-plus-text fusion, [TedRec’s ablations](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18166v1) show degradation when replacing adaptive gating with addition or contextual fusion with itemwise products. However, its text representations use pretrained language models; its “Random” variant is random item text vectors, not a jointly trained random-token encoder. These findings support testing fusion choices, not assuming text automatically helps.

A controlled comparison therefore deserves consideration: unchanged HSTU with ID-only, ID+mean-pooled text, and ID+small CNN text, each one jointly trained model with matched tokenization and budget. Sparse interactions leave rare identifiers weakly supervised; missing descriptions, vocabulary cutoffs, hashing collisions, and truncation can erase specificity before encoding. These are design limitations, not measured findings for these four datasets. Preserve alphanumeric identifiers and units; evaluate attribute-sensitive examples separately from validation HR@10.
